_nota: El Dorado: ceremonia muisca en Guatavita (Juan Rodríguez Freyle, El Carnero, 1636); intento de desagüe de Antonio de Sepúlveda (1580); balsa muisca hallada en 1969 en Pasca, hoy en el Museo del Oro de Bogotá.
dora01-conquistadores: spanish conquistadors in armor exhausted marching through a dense misty jungle, some fallen, golden light rays
dora02-ciudad: a mythical golden city glowing in the middle of a jungle at sunset, golden towers, mist, dreamlike
dora03-hombre: silhouette of an indigenous chief standing alone at the shore of a mountain lake at dawn, mist on the water
dora04-laguna: a round green mountain lagoon surrounded by high Andean hills in Colombia, mist at dawn, aerial view
dora05-polvo: an indigenous chief covered head to toe in shining gold dust, standing on a balsa raft, torches, dark lake at night
dora06-balsa: a reed raft with indigenous priests floating in the middle of a dark lagoon at night, torches, gold objects falling into the water
dora07-mapa: an old parchment treasure map of South America with a golden city drawn on it, candlelight, spanish conquistador hand
dora08-corte: a deep v-shaped notch cut into the rim of a round mountain lagoon, workers with ropes and buckets, 16th century
dora09-balsa-oro: a small intricate pre-columbian gold raft figurine with tiny gold figures of a chief and priests, museum spotlight, black background
dora10-final: silhouette of a golden man standing on a raft on a misty lake at dawn, sun rising behind him
